content.title: Highlights and goals from Chile 4-2 Cape Verde in the FIFA Series
content.text: EVENT ENDEDChile staged a comeback to defeat Cape Verde 4-2 in a thrilling friendly match, marked by Chile's strong second-half performance.Image: VAVEL O jogo no Eden Park chega ao fim! O Chile consegue uma reviravolta impressionante e vence Cabo Verde por 4-2 num confronto repleto de emoções. Após estar em desvantagem, mesmo contra um adversário com dez jogadores, o Chile reagiu de forma brilhante para garantir a vitória. The match at Eden Park has come to an end! Chile staged a stunning comeback to defeat Cape Verde 4-2 in a thrilling match. Despite falling behind against a ten-man opponent, Chile rallied strongly to secure the victory. A deep pass that Cape Verde’s defense struggled to clear; the ball stayed in play after rebounding off the goalkeeper, Chandía tapped it on, and Tapia slotted it home. The match is getting more intense, with Chile trying to break through the defensive wall with mid-range shots and changes of direction. Cape Verde is holding firm, and every turnover is hard-fought; the Africans are looking for the equalizer. GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL GOOOOOOAL, GOOOOOOOOOAL, GOOOOOAL FOR CHILE. The Andean team has scored their third goal and turned the game around, thanks to a great team play that set up Felipe Loyola for a powerful finish inside the box. The match has reached the 64-minute mark, and Chile clearly has the upper hand in possession, though they lack clarity in the final third. The Chilean national team surprises with a dangerous counterattack that ends with a shot that goes wide. Cape Verde responds immediately with a series of crosses into the box, but the opposing defense holds firm despite being a man down. Chile takes complete control of the game with long periods of possession and high pressure as they seek the equalizer. Cape Verde drops back with all its players behind the ball, defending intensely and closing down spaces to hold onto the lead. The second half kicks off at Eden Park with Cape Verde leading 2-1 over Chile in this 2026 FIFA Series friendly. The African side, despite being a man down, is showing discipline and determination, while Chile pushes forward in search of the equalizer. We’re heading into halftime. The African team leads 2–1, having surprised the Chileans with their play. They’ve won the ball back to launch counterattacks, catching Chile off guard. Despite playing with 10 men down the stretch, Cape Verde is beating Chile, which had looked slightly better. GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL GOOOOAL, GOOOOAL, GOOOOAL FOR CAPE VERDE. Down a man, they’re already ahead—a great play down the middle that moved the ball to the left side with several players involved. Sidny Lopes Cabral took the shot and caught the goalkeeper off guard at the near post, making it 2-1. Diney Borges was sent off after handling the ball during a counterattack led by Díaz, leaving Cape Verde down to 10 men. The resulting free kick hit the crossbar; Chile is dominating this final stretch of the first half. GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL GOOOOOAL, GOOOOOAL, GOOOOOAL FOR CAPE VERDE. The equalizer came quickly: a great play down the left flank, a perfect cross from Cabral, no one managed to clear it, and Dailon Rocha Livramento tapped the ball into the net. GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL GOOOOOAL, GOOOOOAL, GOOOOOAL FOR CHILE. The first goal of the match came after a nice move through the middle, with a perfect pass from Echeverría to Ben Brereton Díaz, who finished with a left-footed strike—a great goal from the Derby County player. Cape Verde had the first dangerous chance of the match, with Jorginho Soares firing a shot from outside the box that went just wide of the goal. Chile responded with a quick attack down the right flank that ended with a cross that failed to find a finisher. Chile dominates possession in the opening minutes, moving the ball intelligently and looking for space on the wings.
